liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cryptical Envelopment** (4 reviews): Reviewer says Cryptical signals a strong performance within its first fifteen seconds; Bobby sounds very high-strung on vocals during Cryptical [5][7][12][13]
- **Cosmic Charlie** (1 review): The Other One into Cosmic Charlie is praised as great [10]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-21.sbd.cotsman.17033.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 5 songs; 22 min; rated 2.9/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard quality poor but still listenable; Sound is distorted but listenable; reviewer enjoys the harsh tape character, best played loud; Audio is badly flawed, and Ned's keyboards are hard to find in the mix [4][5][13]
- **gd70-11-21.sbd.hanno.14858.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 22 min; rated 2.4/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound is distorted but listenable; reviewer enjoys the harsh tape character, best played loud [12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the following night's show was reportedly at Middlesex County Community College in Edison, NJ [6]
- A chimp act opened, and the New Riders of the Purple Sage also played [7]
- Ned Lagin reportedly joined on Uncle John's Band, though the setlist order is uncertain [7]
- Reviewer says a chimp act was the first act, rather than the New Riders [8]
- Crowd without tickets burst through the gym doors; reviewer blames duplicate ticket numbers and recalls helping Sam Cutler hold them back [8]
- Reviewer is certain Ned played keyboards at the show [8]
- Ticketless fans surged in through the doors; reviewer saw a policeman go under the crowd and was pushed over a speaker [9]
- Reviewer calls the trained chimps the strangest sight ever seen at a concert, with the New Riders also playing [9]
- Reviewer found this Cosmic Charlie matches the one on a cleaner soundboard from the 1970 Cincinnati Field House show [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-21.sbd.cotsman.17033.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard Partial [1]. Also: Degraded multi-generation soundboard; a splice in Drums likely drops several minutes of music; Minor splice at 2:46 in the first verse of The Other One; A roughly 90-minute audience tape has long been rumored but never surfaced; the uploader suspects it doesn't exist [1]
- **gd70-11-21.sbd.hanno.14858.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Uli Teute and Hanno Bunjes; source: Soundboard Partial [2]. Also: Reviewer wonders who taped this and why only one portion circulates; the rest is missing [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jeff Albertson: [Murder Ballad Monday | "Don't Murder Me..." Dire Wolf](https://singout.org/dont-murder-dire-wolf/) [16]
- Poster by www.digitalcommonwealth.org: [Grateful Dead at Sargent Gym, Boston University: clockwise from front, Ned Lagin, Jerry Garcia, Phil Lesh, Ron "Pigpen" ](https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/search/commonwealth-oai:7m01c792p) [17]
- Fan art by www.digitalcommonwealth.org: [New Riders of the Purple Sage opening for the Grateful Dead at Sargent Gym, Boston University: John 'Marmaduke' Dawson p](https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/search/commonwealth-oai:ff36f3744) [18]
- Poster by www.digitalcommonwealth.org: [Grateful Dead at Sargent Gym, Boston University: The Grateful Dead onstage](https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/search/commonwealth-oai:rn302h900) [19]
- Fan art by www.digitalcommonwealth.org: [Grateful Dead at Sargent Gym, Boston University: Jerry Garcia, Bill Kreutzmann, Phil Lesh, and Bob Weir](https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/search/commonwealth-oai:ff36gp12t) [20]
